headline: Tuesday is sunny but cool and windy, Wednesday is calm and dry, and the next storm brings rain and strong winds on Thursday — though the San Diego area may get only about a quarter inch.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: Morning clouds clear from north to south, and Tuesday turns mostly sunny but cool and breezy, with highs in the upper 60s at the coast and valleys, lower 70s in the low desert, 50s in the High Desert and upper 30s to lower 50s in the mountains, roughly 2–12 degrees below normal. Breezy west winds at the coast and valleys ease after about 7 PM. Winds peak around midday in the mountains and deserts, with gusts of 25–40 mph, topping 40 mph on ridges and through passes and very isolated gusts near 50 mph, before gradually easing late afternoon and evening. Clouds regather along the coast Tuesday night, with a 30–40% chance of a low cloud deck at times, mainly between about 2 and 7 AM Wednesday and most likely around San Diego.

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: Wednesday looks mostly sunny, dry and not windy, but only a couple of degrees warmer. The next storm arrives Thursday morning in Orange and western San Bernardino Counties and moves southeast across the region during the day, bringing rain, a slight chance of thunderstorms and gusts of about 35–50 mph in the mountains and deserts. By the time it moves out early Friday, rain should total a little over an inch in the mountains and the L.A. Basin, less than three-quarters of an inch in San Diego and Riverside Counties, and perhaps only about a quarter inch around San Diego. Snow levels drop to around 6,500 feet as the rain ends, giving Big Bear light snow and a few inches above 7,500 feet, such as the higher ski slopes; Friday then looks fair and dry.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: Saturday looks fair and dry as the storm track takes a pause. Sunday and Monday are very uncertain: it could stay dry, but most computer-model runs bring in a weak system with light rain sometime Sunday, Sunday night or Monday. After that, some runs build an unusually strong area of high pressure over the West that would bring dry and very warm weather ahead of Thanksgiving, while others keep the cool, unsettled and sometimes wet and windy pattern going.

coast: A High Surf Advisory is in effect until 4 AM Wednesday for the Orange County and San Diego County coasts: surf of 6–9 feet with sets to 11 feet on west-facing beaches, with high surf and strong rip currents through midweek. Surf drops briefly to 3–5 feet with sets to 6 feet on Wednesday, then a new northwest swell raises it again Thursday through Friday. Minor coastal flooding is expected at times during high tides this week because of the surf, even with tides under 6.5 feet through Friday; King Tides peak next week, with tides over 7 feet possible starting Saturday, Nov. 21. For boaters, a Small Craft Advisory runs until 4 AM Wednesday with 25–30 knot gusts (near gale force around San Clemente Island) and steep 7–10 ft seas, slowly easing Wednesday morning, before steep 7–10 ft seas and 20–30 knot gusts return Thursday into Friday morning.
watch_for: Thursday's rain amounts around San Diego, which may be only about a quarter inch while areas to the north get more than an inch.
High surf and minor coastal flooding at high tide, with King Tides able to top 7 feet starting Saturday.
Whether Sunday–Monday brings light rain, and whether a very warm, dry spell follows before Thanksgiving.
confidence: Forecasters are confident in a sunny, breezy Tuesday and a dry Wednesday, increasingly confident in the details of Thursday's storm, and very uncertain about Sunday onward.
